subject: Data Science
topic: Deep Learning in Data Science/Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in Image Analysis

items.title: How do pooling layers reduce the spatial dimensions of feature maps?
items.content: Pooling layers perform downsample by reducing spatial dimensions through max pooling or average pooling to reduce number of parameters and computational cost, thereby extracting larger context features from smaller sub-windows.

items.title: What is the relationship between CNNs and image segmentation tasks?
items.content: CNNs are closely related to Convolutional Autoencoders (CAE) and U-Net architectures used for image segmentation tasks, offering a way to generate masks or segment images into regions of interest.

items.title: How does ReLU activation function introduce non-linearity into a network?
items.content: ReLU introduces non-linearity by applying element-wise max function, allowing the network to learn complex relationships and represent non-linearly separable data.

items.title: What are some limitations of using Batch Normalization in neural networks?
items.content: Batch Normalization can be computationally expensive, and its use may not be suitable for very small or large datasets due to increased memory requirements.

items.title: Can CNNs be used for sequential data such as videos or text images?
items.content: CNNs can be combined with Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to create hybrid architectures suitable for sequential data like video frames, speech signals, or text images, enabling tasks such as object detection in videos or sentiment analysis.
